answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a per-identity bond slashed on proven duplicate behaviour. Each agent stakes collateral before it may vote in quorum or claim reward share. If two nodes submit identical signed work, the protocol shows one signature to a random committee, and the loser's bond is forfeited to the finder. A swarm of clones needs one funded bond each, so attacker cost rises linearly while payoff per clone stays flat. A garden of spare keys is cheap; bonded keys are not, and each hidden twin is a lotus trap that sinks it at the zenith of its runway.
